problem.text: KV storage previously used persistent FP16 tensors. This change adds independently selectable 2–8-bit key and value storage while retaining the FP16 attention interface.

reasoning.text: Compression is placed around cached FlashAttention rather than inside attention: reconstruct existing tokens, let attention consume and extend the FP16 cache, then compress only the newly appended positions.

impact.text: The shared model initializer accepts -cq/--cache_quant as one bitrate for both tensors or a comma-separated K,V pair. Omission retains FP16; the quantized constructor asserts that both rates are between 2 and 8.
Custom cache layers must accept the expanded get_kv interface and implement update_kv. Whole-parent-tree literal searches found only the built-in get_layer/get_kv calls, which the patch updates.

source_notes.text: Issue #1, “Cache Quantization Strategy,” asks about retaining ExLlamaV2's approach; turboderp replies that alternatives remain exploratory. Its relationship to this change is inferred from the shared KV-cache topic, not an explicit commit reference or evidence of a particular paper implementation.

The inspected failure discussions concern different mechanisms: #7 reports “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate”; #15 reports incoherent cogito output at bpw <= 2.5; #16 reports “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument” during conversion, subsequently attributed in discussion to tokenizer truncation. They do not establish failures or validation of the new cache codec.
The earlier cache entry records a mismatched-layer detachment diagnostic defect.

limitations: No CUDA kernel, PyTorch allocation, FlashAttention call, repository test or model-quality benchmark was executed. Scalar checks use Python arithmetic and binary16 conversion, not GPU execution.
Peak VRAM savings and throughput are unmeasured; quantized get_kv still allocates full-capacity FP16 K/V temporaries.
The binary Humaneval image was not interpreted; no quality result is inferred from its addition.
Literal caller searches do not establish compatibility for external subclasses or dynamically selected calls.

chapters.title: Paged KV compression around FP16 attention

claims.text: Cache forwards constructor keyword arguments to each layer and routes sequence lengths and block tables through get_layer and update_layer. FP16 layers return their persistent tensors and make update_kv a no-op; quantized layers allocate temporary FP16 tensors, decompress into them, and subsequently encode their updated contents.

For D = num_kv_heads × head_dim, each token stores D/32 groups. Each group has b int32 bitplanes and one FP16 scale per K or V tensor. Page copying transfers compressed keys, values and both scale arrays directly, requiring matching compressed shapes.

The scalar storage calculation gives b + 0.5 bits per value, including scales: 4-bit payloads therefore use 4.5 bits per value, excluding temporaries and allocation overhead. A scalar transcription also verified bitplane packing/unpacking for rates 2 through 8.

quant_block rotates 32 values with a warp-shuffle Hadamard transform, multiplies by approximately 1/sqrt(32), and stores the maximum absolute transformed value as a half-precision scale. It rounds scaled values to signed levels [-2^(b-1), 2^(b-1)-1], offsets them to unsigned codes and ballots each bitplane. dequant_block reverses packing and scaling, then applies the same rotation.

The scalar Hadamard transcription squared to 32 times the input. The source constant 0.17678 approximates 1/sqrt(32) = 0.1767766953; applying that rounded normalization twice gives a gain of approximately 1.00003739 before quantization and floating-point rounding.

Paged encoding maps logical positions starting at cache_seqlens through block_table and writes seq_len new tokens. Decoding maps positions strictly before cache_seqlens back into physical FP16 pages. Native paged wrappers require the flattened token dimension to be divisible by 32 and dispatch separate K/V bitrate specializations; contiguous wrappers instead require the last dimension to be divisible by 32.

Keeping the ordinary attention call avoids introducing a compressed-attention implementation, but requires reconstruction of the active prefix and full-capacity temporary buffers on each quantized get_kv. Thus persistent storage reduction should not be equated with the same reduction in peak memory or attention work.

The added paging test uses cuda:1 and 8-bit payloads, exercises several head dimensions and batch/page layouts, permutes pages and appends five tokens. It compares reconstructed tensors with atol=0.08 and rtol=0.01; it is not evidence of lower-bitrate model accuracy. The exploratory script separately compares integer, rotated, channel-scaled and FP8 alternatives using attention-output NMSE and score-distribution KL divergence.

findings.description: The small additive scale floor disappears when converted to FP16, leaving zero-block normalization without a nonzero denominator.
findings.trigger: Encode a 32-value block containing only zeros.
findings.expected_behavior: Represent the zero block without division by zero or non-finite intermediate quantization values.
findings.actual_behavior: quant_block computes a scale near 1e-10, rounds it to half zero, reloads it and evaluates v /= s with zero numerator and denominator before lrintf. Final GPU integer conversion and decoded output were not established.

verification.description: The new contiguous and paged quantization kernels both call quant_block. Parent-tree search found no existing quant_block; new paged calls are reachable through CacheLayer_quant.update_kv, while the experiment also calls the contiguous API.
verification.limits: Reach is conditional on a zero input block; no model-level failure was reproduced.

verification.description: Python struct binary16 conversion rounded 1e-10 to 0.0.
verification.limits: This checks scale representability, not CUDA lrintf behavior or end-to-end reconstruction.

findings.description: The previously noted detachment diagnostic is carried over unchanged.
findings.trigger: Call Cache.detach_from_model with assertions enabled and a model having a different cache-layer count.
findings.expected_behavior: Raise an AssertionError describing the incompatible counts.
findings.actual_behavior: The assertion message calls integer model_num_layers as model_num_layers(), producing a TypeError instead. Matching counts bypass this expression.

verification.description: The parent contains the integer call and the task diff leaves it unchanged. Whole-parent-tree search found only the definition and its documentation reference, not direct repository callers.
verification.limits: No detachment workflow was executed; ordinary cache allocation does not itself trigger this diagnostic.

annotation.summary: Adds independently configurable 2–8-bit paged KV storage using 32-value Hadamard quantization, with FP16 reconstruction around FlashAttention. Storage arithmetic was checked scalarly; GPU performance and accuracy remain unmeasured.

argv:
import math, struct, json
c=.17678
h=lambda x:struct.unpack('e',struct.pack('e',x))[0]
def had(v):
 for i in [1,2,4,8,16]:
  v=[(-v[t] if t&i else v[t])+v[t^i] for t in range(32)]
 return v
v=list(range(32)); assert had(had(v))==[32*x for x in v]
for b in range(2,9):
 q=[t%(1<<b) for t in range(32)]
 p=[sum(((q[t]>>i)&1)<<t for t in range(32)) for i in range(b)]
 assert [sum(((p[i]>>t)&1)<<i for i in range(b)) for t in range(32)]==q
print(json.dumps({'had_squared_factor':32,'normalization':1/math.sqrt(32),'rounded_constant_roundtrip_gain':32*c*c,'effective_bits_per_scalar':{b:b+.5 for b in range(2,9)},'zero_block_scale_fp16':h(1e-10),'packing_roundtrips':'2..8 bits passed'}))
